title: GPU fleet fidelity scaling lens — quantization & batching sensitivity sheet
content:
Purpose:
A compact operational worksheet for sizing regional GPU fleets under a ‘fidelity-scaling’ lens: quantify throughput gains from lower-precision execution and larger batching, then map those gains to fleet counts while accounting for quality impact (semantic drift / similarity loss) and latency SLOs. This is an intentionally lightweight, working sheet for infra/product tradeoffs — not a final procurement doc.

Context / Why this exists:
- Increasing customer traffic + multi-region growth requires tighter tradeoffs between unit cost and model fidelity.
- We need a single-pane sensitivity view that translates quant/batch knobs into estimated GPUs required by region and highlights where quality regressions exceed product thresholds.
- This sheet focuses on production-serving characteristics (steady-state throughput + short surges) rather than offline training.

Key assumptions (editable inputs):
- Baseline model: LLM-XL-13B (instruction-tuned) served with FP16 on H100 (baseline fidelity).
- Typical request token distribution: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65–512 tokens), 10% long (>512 tokens). Effective avg sequence length used in calc = 220 tokens.
- Latency SLOs: P95 <= 220ms for interactive endpoints, P95 <= 800ms for batch/rerank endpoints.
- Cache behavior: KV cache hit rate variable (0%–60%). Default scenario uses 30% hit.
- Workload: Global peak token ingress = 220M tokens/hour (~61k tokens/sec). Peak regional split (provisional): us-west 45%, eu-central 30%, ap-southeast 25%.

GPU / quant / batching perf model (editable table):
Columns: GPU | Precision | Batch sizes modeled | Effective tokens/sec per GPU (avg seq=220, kv_hit=30%) | Quality delta (embedding cosine drop vs FP16 baseline)
- H100 | FP16 | 1, 4, 16 | Baseline per-gpu = 4,200 t/s @ batch1; batch4 ~6,800 t/s; batch16 ~9,500 t/s | 0.0%
- H100 | 8-bit (GPTQ-like) | 1, 4, 16 | 1.35x FP16 throughput -> 5,670 / 9,180 / 12,825 t/s | -0.6% avg similarity
- H100 | 4-bit (AWQ) | 1, 4, 16 | 1.7x FP16 -> 7,140 / 11,560 / 16,150 t/s | -2.4% avg similarity (tails larger for long contexts)
- A100 | FP16 | 1, 4, 16 | Baseline per-gpu = 2,900 / 4,700 / 6,600 t/s | 0.0%
- L4  | INT8 (edge) | 1, 4, 16 | 900 / 1,800 / 2,700 t/s | -3.5% (higher semantic drift on instruction prompts)

How throughput numbers were derived (model):
- tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = base_fp16_tps * quant_scale * batch_scale * (1 + kv_hit_rate * kv_factor)
- kv_factor is modeled as incremental throughput improvement from repeated prefix cache (default kv_factor=0.22).
- Batch_scale measured from internal microbench runs (nonlinear, diminishing returns after batch=32).

Sample sensitivity scenarios (snapshots):
1) Conservative fidelity (FP16 everywhere, no quant):
   - Global required H100 equiv GPUs = ceil(peak_tokens_sec / 4,200) = ceil(61,000 / 4,200) = 15 H100s (baseline)
   - Regional split: us-west 7, eu-central 5, ap-southeast 3 (rounded)
   - Notes: Quality preserved; cost highest; autoscale headroom minimal for 2x surge.
2) Moderate quant adoption (8-bit where acceptable; batch 4 for interactive):
   - Effective per-gpu token/sec (us avg) ~ 9,180 (H100 8-bit batch4)
   - Global required = ceil(61,000 / 9,180) = 7 H100-equivalent GPUs
   - Reg allocation: us-west 4, eu-central 2, ap-southeast 1
   - Quality: −0.6% embedding similarity; flagged prompt classes (code, math) show larger deltas — see Appendix.
3) Aggressive packing (4-bit + batch16 for non-interactive routes; hybrid lanes):
   - Use mixing: interactive endpoints remain 8-bit batch4; non-interactive heavy throughput uses 4-bit batch16.
   - Effective blended throughput reduces global GPU need to 4–5 H100-equivalents.
   - Quality: average -1.8% but some tails > -4% for reasoning prompts.

Fidelity bands & product thresholds (recommended):
- Band A (no quant): baseline quality; use for customers with strict fidelity SLAs or for endpoints with high-risk outputs (legal, finance).
- Band B (8-bit): acceptable for majority of chat features; requires per-prompt validation & eval suite pass (drift <1%).
- Band C (4-bit): use only for cached, rerank, or sanitized pipelines with fallback to Band A for failcases.

Regional fleet mapping (working recommendation):
Inputs: projected peak, acceptable fidelity band selection per product team. Example mapping for Moderate quant adoption (Band B primary):
- us-west (45%): target capacity = 0.45 * 61,000 = 27,450 t/s -> 3 H100-8bit-batch4 (3 x 9,180 = 27,540) -> recommend 3 H100-equivalent + 1 warm spare
- eu-central (30%): 18,300 t/s -> 2 H100-8bit-batch4 (2 x 9,180 = 18,360) -> recommend 2 H100-equivalent + 1 warm spare if SLA critical
- ap-southeast (25%): 15,250 t/s -> 2 H100-8bit-batch4 (2 x 9,180 = 18,360) but capacity > needed -> can drop to 1 H100 + 1 A100 for mixed fleet (cost-opt)
Notes: "H100-equivalent" means normalized throughput; physical fleet mix can include A100 / L4 with capacity multipliers.

Surge and fallback policy (operational):
- Surge policy: automatic cross-region burst up to 20% by routing to adjacent region; must only route to capacity-marked Band B or A instances depending on request classification.
- Fallback lanes: if quantized variant fails quality checks on a sampled response (per 1k responses), auto-fallback the user session to FP16 for the next N requests. Log and create incident if rate > 0.5%.
- Warm spares: maintain 1 warm spare per region for median-sized fleets; for small regions maintain 1 shared warm pool.

Loss vs cost sensitivity quick view (editable):
- Rough cost multiple: 8-bit runtime ≈ 0.72x of FP16 cost per token; 4-bit runtime ≈ 0.55x (estimates include memory and utilization effects).
- ROIC breakpoint: when traffic > ~1.8x baseline, investing in 8-bit rollouts typically pays back within 6–12 weeks due to lower infra costs.

Appendix: Prompt-level quality hotspots (notes from eval runs):
- Instruction-following open-ended multi-step planning tasks show larger quality regression under 4-bit (coherent chaining decays).
- Code synthesis: 8-bit often safe; 4-bit introduces reproducible defects at longer sequences (>400 tokens).
- Rerank/embedding-based UX: embedding cosine delta correlates with rerank MRR drop (~0.8% similarity drop -> ~1.5% MRR loss).

Action items / next steps (owner initials):
- (Aisha) Lock down product fidelity bands per endpoint (deadline: 2029-12-01).
- (Marco) Run 10k-sample eval for 8-bit vs FP16 on code/math prompt set and produce report (JIRA-INF-1248) due 2029-12-08.
- (Emily) Add per-route tracing flags to measure live quality drift and link to rollback automation (PR #5123).
- (Dmitri) Prototype warm-spare autoscale runbook and test cross-region routing with synthetic surge (target: Q1 2030).

Open questions / risks:
- What is the acceptable per-customer quality SLA degradation (explicit threshold)? Product needs to sign off.
- Hot-path prompts that are highly sensitive (legal/cust data) must bypass quant lanes; we need a tagging approach.
- Observability: need a low-latency semantic-similarity metric for live traffic to detect drift inside 1 minute.

Version history:
- v0.1 (2029-11-15) initial draft with baseline numbers and sensitivity lanes.
- v0.2 (2030-02-10) added mixed-fleet mapping and cost multiplies (Marco).
- v0.3 (2030-04-02) updated throughput lines after microbench re-run; added action items (Emily, Dmitri).

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet intentionally favors clarity over micro-accuracy. Replace the throughput constants with your exact bench results in the top table before using for procurement.
- When editing, keep the top Key assumptions block updated — all downstream numbers are derived from it.

Raw calc snippet (for copy into sheet):
- peak_tokens_sec = total_tokens_hour / 3600
- region_tokens_sec = peak_tokens_sec * region_share
- gpus_needed = ceil(region_tokens_sec / effective_tps_per_gpu)

End of sheet.
